full_judgment:
21. It can be, also, profitably observed that though sad, yet it is a fact that people do not hesitate in resorting to vengeance over the unfortunate death of their near and dear ones. There is a tendency to rope in as many people as possible for facing trial in respect of death or injury of unfortunate victim. It has been found that on occasion’s innocent persons including the aged, infirm, ladies and children are booked for standing on the dock and remain confined in custody till pendency of cases. Some are acquitted by Court of First Instance and some by Appellate Court but only after languishing in confinement for years. Such efforts on the part of unscrupulous survivors of crime or relatives of the victim invariably, but unfortunately, help the real culprits as it becomes difficult on the part of Court/ /Tribunal to sift grain out of chaff. Under such circumstances and in view of prevalent Criminal Jurisprudential System in the country, the doctrine of presumption of innocence in favour of the accused makes Justice System itself a victim which ultimately weakens the Criminal Justice Dispensation System. In cases of group clashes involving a number of persons as accused a balanced approach by Court is required to be insisted so that neither an innocent person should be convicted nor a guilty person be acquitted. Every case in the final analysis would depend upon its own fact. 

 102. Every Criminal trial is an odyssey of discovery in which truth is the quest. It is the duty of prosecution to explore every avenue open to it in order to unveil truth and bring to book the real offenders and to advance cause of justice. Witnesses who can throw sufficient light in unfolding truth are to be produced before witness box by prosecution witnesses. Witnesses, as Bantham said, are eyes and ears or Justice. Non-examination of material witnesses shall give rise to a strong presumption against prosecution case in respect of involvement of an accused in the felony allegedly committed by him. If a material witness who would unroll the genesis of incident is not convincingly brought to fore otherwise or where there is a gap or infirmity in the prosecution case which could have been supplied or provided by examining a witness who, though, available is not examined, prosecution case can be termed as suffering from a serious deficiency and infirmity and withholding of such a material and vital witness would oblige the court to draw an adverse inference against the prosecution by holding that if the witness would have been examined he would not have supported the prosecution case as projected. 

 103. It emerged from the evidence of Informant PW 1 and other prosecution witnesses that deceased had mother, wife, full brothers, uncle, maternal uncle and close relations. It, also, came to light that at Baraipara Bazar there had been many shops and shop-keepers had been in the shop. Inquest Report reveals that Mostafa Kamal, Sheikh Amirul, Abdus Samad Sheikh, Md Tutul Molla, Md Moshier, Munir Sheikh, Md Abdullah, Uncle, cousin, uncle, cousin, maternal uncle, cousin and younger brother respectively were signatories to Inquest Report. From the evidence of PW 17, Investigating Officer, it has been manifested that, Mostafa Kamal, Sheikh Amirul, Tutul Molla, Moshier, Munir Sheikh and Md Abdullah are uncle, brother, uncle, cousin brother, maternal uncle, cousin brother and full brother respectively of deceased Bahauddin. Index/site plan demonstrates that near about the place of occurrence there had been eighteen (18) shops, one mosque and one medicine shop but the mother, wife, brother, uncle, maternal uncle, cousin brother, shop-keepers adjacent to the place of occurrence were not at all examined by prosecution in regard to embroilment of convict-appellants in the crime. Failure to produce vital witnesses and best evidence before the court without any explanation and reason in the background and fact and circumstances of the case was a serious reflection and fatal to the fabric of prosecution case and an adverse inference against prosecution case for non-examination of the above witnesses legitimately might arise and virtually arose. The inevitable legal presumption is that if the witnesses and persons stated above would have been examined they would not have definitely supported the prosecution case in abridgment of convict-appellants in causing the fall of deceased Bahauddin Sheikh. On this score, convict-appellants are entitled to get the benefit of doubt.
